rationale: Billed: Line 1 CPT 45385, Colonoscopy with removal of tumor(s)/polyp(s) by snare technique. Medical record documentation: Operative Note documents the procedure performed as "Colonoscopy with snare polypectomy x2" and gives contemporaneous, specific intraoperative detail that two polyps (6 mm ascending, 4 mm sigmoid) were identified and removed using snare technique with immediate retrieval and confirmed hemostasis (Operative Note, p.25-26; cf. intraop timeline). The Anatomic Pathology report documents two separately labeled specimens submitted as hot snare polypectomy specimens with measured sizes (Ascending: 0.6 x 0.5 x 0.3 cm; Sigmoid: 0.4 x 0.4 x 0.3 cm) (Pathology Report, p.37). The retrieved APC policy rows did not contain a targeted policy rule that imposes additional, unmet documentation requirements for CPT 45385 (policy row returned notes that there is No is_target=true PolicyRule for code='45385'). Together, the contemporaneous operative description (technique: snare; two polyps removed and retrieved separately), intraoperative timeline, and pathology specimen labeling/sizes support billing CPT 45385 as submitted. Key supporting documentation: Operative Note (Operative Note) p.25 (procedure performed; technique and lesions), Operative Note p.25 (description of snare removal of 6 mm and 4 mm polyps), Pathology Report p.37 (specimen descriptions and sizes), and the retrieved policy row noting no direct target rule for 45385. Conclusion: the medical record documents the snare polypectomy(s) performed as billed and there is no retrieved policy requirement contradicted by the record; determination = No Finding. Billed: CPT 99152 (Moderate sedation, first 15 minutes) on claim APC-2026-58317 for patient MRN-3391847. The medical record documents physician-directed, RN-administered moderate (conscious) sedation that began at 07:25 and continued through scope withdrawal/hand-off, with continuous monitoring and medication administration consistent with moderate sedation. Operative Note documents moderate sedation start time (Operative Note, SECTION 8 OF 13, p.25: Moderate sedation administered beginning at 07:25) and directs reviewer to the sedation flowsheet (NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_03.pdf-n25, p.25). Medication Administration Record shows sedative/analgesic administrations at 07:25 (Midazolam 2 mg; Fentanyl 50 mcg) and titration at 07:35 (Medication Administration Record, p.30-31). Intraoperative Record documents anesthesia induction and monitoring consistent with moderate sedation and shows case times (Anesthesia Induction Initiated 07:18; scope insertion 07:32; scope withdrawal 08:06; patient out of OR 08:10) (Intraoperative Record - Anesthesia & Circulating Nurse, p.22-24). Governing APC policy concept emphasizes that intra-service sedation time is measured from administration of sedating agent(s) to recovery-readiness on the sedation flowsheet and that reviewers should reconcile the flowsheet to the scope timer (APC Coding Concept - Moderate Sedation Add-On Time, RULE-Policy-Documents-APC-APC_Policy_Concepts.xlsx-APC-03-4). Reconciliation here is satisfied: the operative note states sedation began at 07:25, MAR documents sedative administration at 07:25 with subsequent titration, and intraoperative/operative timing shows the patient was under monitored sedation through scope withdrawal and transfer to PACU (07:25 -> ~08:06-08:10), which exceeds the initial 15-minute interval required for 99152. Therefore the documentation supports the billed 99152 as submitted (No Finding). Evidence: Operative Note p.25 (sedation start 07:25), Medication Administration Record p.30 (07:25 meds), Intraoperative Record p.22-24 (monitoring, case times), APC policy concept text (sedation time measured from administration to recovery-readiness). Billed: Line 2 = 99152 (moderate sedation, first 15 min); Lines 3-4 = two units of 99153 (moderate sedation, same physician, each additional 15 min). Governing policy requires that sedation intra-service time be measured from administration of the sedating agent to recovery-readiness, and that the midpoint of each additional 15-minute increment must be reached to support each 99153 unit (policy: midpoint ≈ 23 minutes for the first add-on; subsequent add-on midpoints follow sequentially) (RULE-Policy-Documents-APC-APC_Policy_Concepts.xlsx-APC-03-4, p. [concept]). Documentation: the operative note documents that moderate sedation was administered beginning at 07:25 (Operative Note, NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_03.pdf-n25, p.25) and the Medication Administration Record shows sedative agents given at 07:25 (Midazolam 2 mg; Fentanyl 50 mcg) with additional Midazolam at 07:35 (Medication Administration Record, NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_03.pdf-n31, p.30-31). The end/procedure timing shows scope insertion at 07:32 and scope withdrawal at 08:06 with patient out of the OR at 08:10 (Intraoperative Record, NOTE-APC-medical-records-MR_APC_03.pdf-n24, pp.22-24). Measured from documented sedation start (07:25) to the end-of-procedure/transfer times (≈08:06-08:10) yields approximately 41-45 minutes of intra-service moderate sedation, which exceeds the midpoints required to support two additional 15-minute units (first add-on midpoint ≈23 minutes; second add-on midpoint ≈38 minutes). The sedation administration times (MAR) reconcile with the scope timer and intraoperative timeline (operative note and intraop record) as advised by policy. On this three-way check (claim lines vs. record vs. policy), the medical record supports the two billed 99153 units in addition to 99152. Therefore, no correction is required. Billed line: CPT 99153 (additional 15-minute moderate sedation unit), line 4 on claim APC-2026-58317. Governing policy (APC-03) requires the sedation intra-service interval to be measured on the sedation flowsheet (sedation start = administration of sedating agent(s); end = when recovery-readiness/hand-off criteria are met) and further states that the midpoint of the first additional 15-minute increment (approximately 23 total minutes) must be reached to support the first 99153 unit (i.e. you cannot substitute scope insertion-to-withdrawal equipment timers for the sedation flowsheet) (ev1). The medical record's sedation documentation shows sedating medications administered beginning at 07:25 (Midazolam 2 mg and Fentanyl 50 mcg, with a titration midazolam 1 mg at 07:35) (ev2), and the circulating RN documents that recovery-readiness criteria were met at 07:43 with no further sedation after 07:43 (ev3). That sequence yields an intra-service sedation interval of ~07:25-07:43 = 18 minutes by the sedation flowsheet, which is shorter than the policy's ~23 minutes required to support the first 99153 add-on unit. The operative/endoscopy equipment timer shows scope insertion at 07:32 and withdrawal at 08:06 (34 minutes), but the APC policy explicitly differentiates the sedation flowsheet from scope/equipment timers and requires reconciliation in favor of the flowsheet for 99153 (ev4, ev1). Therefore the documentation does not support this billed 99153 additional unit (line 4) - it documents less than the required midpoint/time on the sedation flowsheet. Action: remove this 99153 line (no substitute code for this line) because the record supports only the primary moderate sedation unit (99152) for the sedation interval documented. Evidence used: ev1 (policy), ev2 (med administration times), ev3 (nursing flowsheet/recovery-readiness), ev4 (operative scope timer noted but not acceptable substitute per policy).

evidence.quote: PROCEDURE PERFORMED: Colonoscopy with snare polypectomy x2
In the ascending colon, a 6 mm sessile polyp was identified and removed in its entirety using hot snare technique in a single pass, with immediate retrieval for pathology.
In the sigmoid colon, a second, 4 mm pedunculated polyp was identified and similarly removed via hot snare with immediate retrieval.
SPECIMEN A (Ascending colon): One tan-pink sessile mucosal fragment measuring 0.6 x 0.5 x 0.3 cm.
SPECIMEN B (Sigmoid colon): One tan-pink pedunculated mucosal fragment with a short stalk, measuring 0.4 x 0.4 x 0.3 cm.

Moderate sedation was administered by the circulating RN per standing order beginning at 0725 (see moderate sedation flowsheet, nursing intraop documentation, for administration and monitoring detail).
07:25 | Midazolam | 2 mg | IV | Moderate sedation induction | RN Boyd (order: Dr. Desai)
07:25 | Fentanyl | 50 mcg | IV | Moderate sedation / analgesia | RN Boyd (order: Dr. Desai)
Anesthesia Induction Initiated | 07:18 | Moderate (conscious) sedation — physician-directed, RN-administered — per anesthesia provider

Moderate sedation was administered by the circulating RN per standing order beginning at 0725 (see moderate sedation flowsheet, nursing intraop documentation, for administration and monitoring detail).
07:25 | Midazolam | 2 mg | IV | Moderate sedation induction | RN Boyd (order: Dr. Desai)
07:35 | Midazolam | 1 mg | IV | Sedation titration during procedure | RN Boyd (order: Dr. Desai)
Incision / Procedure Start Time | 07:32 (scope insertion, per endoscopy suite automated procedure timer log)
Closure / Procedure End Time | 08:06 (scope withdrawal, per endoscopy suite automated procedure timer log)
Patient Out of Operating Room | 08:10 | Hemodynamically stable; transferred to PACU

07:25 | Midazolam | 2 mg | IV | Moderate sedation induction | RN Boyd (order: Dr. Desai) 07:25 | Fentanyl | 50 mcg | IV | Moderate sedation / analgesia | RN Boyd (order: Dr. Desai) 07:35 | Midazolam | 1 mg | IV | Sedation titration during procedure | RN Boyd (order: Dr. Desai)

Midazolam 2 mg IV and Fentanyl 50 mcg IV administered at 0725 per Dr. Desai's order, followed by an additional Midazolam 1 mg IV titration dose at 0735 for continued patient movement/discomfort. Patient monitored continuously per moderate sedation protocol (continuous pulse oximetry, cardiac monitor, automated BP q5min, capnography, and periodic verbal responsiveness checks) by circulating RN Boyd throughout the case. Recovery-readiness criteria (stable vital signs, purposeful response to verbal stimuli, protective airway reflexes intact) were met at 0743. No further sedation medication was given after 0743, and the patient remained in a light, arousable sedation state through completion of the procedure and scope withdrawal.

policy_citations.quote: Moderate sedation intra-service time begins at administration of the sedating agent(s) and ends when the patient meets recovery-readiness/hand-off criteria (stable vital signs, purposeful response to verbal stimuli, intact protective airway reflexes), per CPT moderate sedation reporting guidance. This interval is measured on the sedation flowsheet maintained by the administering clinician and is distinct from any endoscopy-suite equipment timer logging scope insertion-to-withdrawal time, which reflects instrument dwell time, not sedation administration. The midpoint of each additional 15-minute increment (approximately 23 total minutes for the first add-on unit) must be reached to support billing that unit of 99153; reviewers should reconcile the sedation flowsheet against any equipment-timer entries elsewhere in the chart before accepting billed 99153 units.

rationale_letter: Re: Audit of claim APC-2026-58317 (patient MRN-3391847) - CPT 99153 (additional moderate sedation unit) - Finding Dear Provider, We have completed a focused audit of line 4 on claim APC-2026-58317 for patient MRN-3391847, which billed CPT 99153 (Moderate sedation services provided by the same physician performing the diagnostic/therapeutic service; each additional 15 minutes intra-service time). The governing APC policy (APC-03) requires that intra-service moderate sedation time be measured on the sedation flowsheet (from administration of sedating agent(s) until recovery-readiness/hand-off criteria are met) and that the midpoint of the first additional 15-minute increment (approximately 23 minutes total) be reached to justify billing a 99153 add-on unit (ev1). The policy further cautions that endoscopy suite equipment timers (scope insertion-to-withdrawal) reflect instrument dwell time and are not a substitute for the sedation flowsheet (ev1). Basis for Finding: - The medication administration record documents sedating agents given at 07:25 (Midazolam 2 mg and Fentanyl 50 mcg) with a titration dose of Midazolam at 07:35 (ev2). - The circulating RN documents that recovery-readiness criteria were met at 07:43 and that no further sedation medication was given after 07:43 (ev3). Measured on the sedation flowsheet, the intra-service sedation interval is therefore approximately 07:25-07:43 = 18 minutes. - The policy requires approximately 23 minutes to reach the midpoint needed to support the first 99153 add-on unit; the documented sedation interval (18 minutes) does not meet that criterion (ev1). The scope insertion-to-withdrawal timer is 07:32-08:06 (34 minutes) (ev4), but APC policy specifies that scope/equipment timers are not equivalent to the sedation flowsheet for reporting 99153 and must not be used as a substitute (ev1). Correction Being Made: - Line 4 (CPT 99153) is not supported by the sedation flowsheet documentation and will be removed. The documentation supports the initial moderate sedation unit CPT 99152 only. If you believe additional documentation exists that documents intra-service sedation time on the administering clinician's sedation flowsheet meeting the policy's midpoint requirement (for example, a sedation flowsheet entry showing sedation start before 07:25 or recovery-readiness later than 07:48 such that >=~23 minutes of sedation is documented), please supply that specific flowsheet entry referencing the patient/chart and the time entries for reconsideration. Absent such evidence, the billed 99153 unit at line 4 is unsupported and will be disallowed. Sincerely, Clinical Claims Audit Team
